RFC8669-3-1.note: Re-judged after the D-8 fix (applyFactsNextHop records Remove{5,6} on code 40; prefixSIDNextHopHandler rewrites the attribute per route). Clause 'ignored': message/rfc8669_test.go::TestRFC8669UnknownTLVIsIgnored pins RFC7606ActionNone and intact bytes for an unallocated TLV (no discrimination record; supplementary). Clause 'propagated unmodified': reactor TestRFC8669UnknownTLVPropagatedAcrossANextHopChange reads attribute 40 on the wire over both relay rails (forwardUpdateCore, reactorForwardRS): positive, next hop unchanged, [LabelIndex, L3 Svc, type 200, L2 Svc, SRGB] byte-identical; negative (R1b: the input that used to violate), next-hop-self with NEXT_HOP really 10.0.0.254, attribute == LabelIndex+type200+SRGB byte-identical in received order. Observed red: positive with applyFactsNextHop broken, negative with prefixSIDNextHopHandler broken. Buffers isolated (well-formed TLVs, only type 200 unknown). Re-judged 2026-10-14 (independent reader, after 8c1c4013f2 and 7d37dcd562). Two covers added, judged against Section 3 ('unknown TLVs MUST be ignored and propagated unmodified'): reactor TestClearTransmittedLabelIndexOnlyOnLabeledUnicast asserts that a body whose Label-Index TLV carries Reserved A5 and Flags 5AFF on IPv4 VPN, where the TLV is unrecognized, leaves clearTransmittedLabelIndex octet-equal (the egress clear only); test/plugin/prefixsid-malformed-receive.ci frame (f) relays an IPv4 VPN Label-Index with Reserved AA and Flags BBCC octet-equal through the daemon. The earlier covers are unchanged. Verdict unchanged. Rejudged 2026-10-16 (independent reader) after the owner-approved 2026-10-16 change ("5 RFC") to test/plugin/prefixsid-malformed-receive.ci: the only edit is frame (b2), the relayed MP_UNREACH_NLRI for 10.0.2.0/24 RD 65001:1 on IPv4 VPN, whose 3-octet label field now pins 800000 in place of the received 007D01, plus its comment; every other action and expect line is byte-identical. RFC 8277 Section 2.4: "Upon transmission, the Compatibility field SHOULD be set to 0x800000. Upon reception, the value of the Compatibility field MUST be ignored." This row rests on frame (f) (Label-Index with Reserved AA and Flags BBCC relayed octet-equal) and on the Go units, none of which changed; (b2) is a withdrawal carrying no attribute 40, so the edit cannot touch the unknown-TLV relay evidence. RFC 8669 Section 3: "For future extensibility, unknown TLVs MUST be ignored and propagated unmodified." Verdict stands.

RFC8669-3.1-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-14 (independent reader, after 8c1c4013f2 and 7d37dcd562). RFC 8669 Section 3.1: 'It MUST be ignored when received for other BGP AFI/SAFI combinations.' The RA33 finding (the parser refused a Label-Index whose length is not 7 on every family, and no tagged unit fed one off labeled unicast through validation or decode) is answered by the new covers: message TestRFC8669LabelIndexAnyLengthIgnoredOffLabeledUnicast asserts RFC7606ActionNone for a 6-octet Label-Index on IPv4 VPN and IPv6 unicast; attribute TestParsePrefixSIDAcceptsOffFamilyLabelIndexLength asserts ParsePrefixSID accepts it, re-emits it octet-equal and renders it attribute-not-implemented-1; reactor TestClearTransmittedLabelIndexOnlyOnLabeledUnicast asserts the egress clear leaves an IPv4 unicast body octet-equal; prefixsid-malformed-receive.ci frame (c) relays the 6-octet TLV on IPv4 VPN octet-equal; the pool test still asserts the SRv6 extractor ignores it. The producer ClassifyPrefixSID skips type 1 and 3 TLVs off labeled unicast without judging their length. Single-polarity stands: there is no Label-Index behavior off labeled unicast to drive negatively. Not asserted: a 7-octet Label-Index off labeled unicast through the JSON formatter. Rejudged 2026-10-16 (independent reader) after the owner-approved 2026-10-16 change ("5 RFC") to test/plugin/prefixsid-malformed-receive.ci: the only edit is frame (b2), the relayed MP_UNREACH_NLRI for 10.0.2.0/24 RD 65001:1 on IPv4 VPN, whose 3-octet label field now pins 800000 in place of the received 007D01, plus its comment; every other action and expect line is byte-identical. RFC 8277 Section 2.4: "Upon transmission, the Compatibility field SHOULD be set to 0x800000. Upon reception, the value of the Compatibility field MUST be ignored." This row rests on frame (c) (6-octet Label-Index on IPv4 VPN relayed octet-equal) and on the Go units, none of which changed; (b2) carries no attribute 40. RFC 8669 Section 3.1: "It MUST be ignored when received for other BGP AFI/SAFI combinations." Verdict stands, single-polarity unchanged.

RFC8669-3.1-3.note: RFC 8669 §3.1 whole field sentence: "RESERVED: 8-bit field. It MUST be clear on transmission and MUST be ignored on reception." This row owns the transmission clause; reception remains RFC8669-3.1-4. Both internal/component/bgp/config/rfc8669_test.go tagged units (TestRFC8669LabelIndexTLVReservedAndFlagsClearOnTransmission and TestRFC8669SRGBFormLabelIndexReservedAndFlagsClearOnTransmission) pin the reserved octet and independent bare-index/SRGB encoders internal/core/bgp/attribute/prefixsid.go::EncodePrefixSID/parsePrefixSIDWithSRGB. internal/component/bgp/reactor/rfc8669_label_index_transmit_test.go::TestRFC8669LabelIndexTransmissionClearsReservedAndFlags separately supplies clean and dirty Label-Index values to raw, whole-packet, parsed, filter-override, general and route-server paths, then checks exact attribute bytes on the real session writer. clearTransmittedLabelIndex in session_prefix_sid.go clears only the bounded type-1 fields in an owned outgoing buffer; session_write.go invokes it after policy. Whole-value equality also requires unchanged unknown TLV, Originator SRGB, source buffer and NLRI. These distinct input cases fail if a dirty Reserved octet escapes or normalization corrupts adjacent content. This repairs the earlier origination-only proof limitation. No SRv6 SID allocation, transposition, VPP or RFC9252 feature claim follows; no runtime result asserted. Re-judged 2026-10-14 (independent reader, after 8c1c4013f2 and 7d37dcd562). The transmit test now builds an IPv4 labeled-unicast route (rfc8669LabeledUnicastBody), the family Section 3.1 defines the TLV for, with the same exact-bytes assertions; the new TestClearTransmittedLabelIndexOnlyOnLabeledUnicast asserts the Reserved octet cleared on IPv4 and IPv6 labeled unicast with attribute 40 before and after MP_REACH_NLRI. Verdict unchanged.

RFC8669-3.1-4.note: Transmission: every EncodePrefixSID shape (bare, all-ones index, SRGB-leading) has Label-Index Reserved 0. Reception: Reserved 0xFF gives Action None, no discard, bytes unchanged, ParsePrefixSID ok. Judge break (Reserved 1 in the SRGB-path encoder): red.

RFC8669-3.1-5.note: RFC 8669 §3.1 whole field sentence: "Flags: 16 bits of flags. None are defined by this document. The Flags field MUST be clear on transmission and MUST be ignored on reception." This row owns transmission; reception remains RFC8669-3.1-6. internal/component/bgp/config/rfc8669_test.go::TestRFC8669LabelIndexTLVReservedAndFlagsClearOnTransmission and TestRFC8669SRGBFormLabelIndexReservedAndFlagsClearOnTransmission assert both Flags octets zero for internal/core/bgp/attribute/prefixsid.go::EncodePrefixSID and parsePrefixSIDWithSRGB. The clean/dirty subcases of internal/component/bgp/reactor/rfc8669_label_index_transmit_test.go::TestRFC8669LabelIndexTransmissionClearsReservedAndFlags drive six final writer/relay paths, including filter overrides, and demand the full expected Prefix-SID with Flags 0000. session_prefix_sid.go::clearTransmittedLabelIndex and its session_write.go callers operate only on owned outgoing bytes after policy. Exact source, unknown-TLV, SRGB and NLRI preservation isolates the type-1 normalization from unrelated dropping or rewriting. Genuine clean and nonzero cases distinguish both polarities; this is no longer only a configuration-encoder assertion. RFC8669 explicitly defers SRv6 data-plane behavior, so this verdict grants no SRv6/VPP implementation scope. Runtime proof remains the parent recorder responsibility. Re-judged 2026-10-14 (independent reader, after 8c1c4013f2 and 7d37dcd562). The transmit test now builds an IPv4 labeled-unicast route, with the same exact-bytes assertions (Flags 0000); the new TestClearTransmittedLabelIndexOnlyOnLabeledUnicast asserts Flags cleared on IPv4 and IPv6 labeled unicast. Verdict unchanged.

RFC8669-3.1-6.note: Same unit: Label-Index Flags 0 on every encoded shape; received Flags 0xFFFF ignored with bytes unchanged and ParsePrefixSID ok.

RFC8669-3.2-1.note: Non-compliant behaviour: non-zero Originator SRGB Flags emitted. config/rfc8669_test.go::TestRFC8669OriginatorSRGBTLVFlagsClearOnTransmission asserts require.Equal([]byte{0,0}, srgb[3:5]) on EncodePrefixSID output. Single-polarity marker present.

RFC8669-3.2-2.note: Same unit: SRGB Flags 0 on send including all-ones base/range; received SRGB Flags 0xFFFF ignored, bytes unchanged (the assertion the earlier note missed). Judge break (SRGB Flags 1): red.

RFC8669-3.2-4.note: Re-judged 2026-10-14 (independent reader, after 8c1c4013f2 and 7d37dcd562). RFC 8669 Section 3.2: 'It MUST be ignored when received for other BGP AFI/SAFI combinations.' The RA33 finding (the parser refused an Originator SRGB whose length is not 2 + 6N on every family, untested off labeled unicast) is answered: message TestRFC8669SRGBAnyLengthIgnoredOffLabeledUnicast asserts RFC7606ActionNone for a 3-octet SRGB on IPv4 VPN; attribute TestParsePrefixSIDAcceptsOffFamilyLabelIndexLength asserts ParsePrefixSID accepts it, re-emits it octet-equal and renders it attribute-not-implemented-3; the pool test asserts the SRv6 extractor ignores it. ClassifyPrefixSID judges SRGB length on labeled unicast only. Single-polarity stands. Not asserted: an end-to-end relay of an SRGB off labeled unicast.

RFC8669-4-1.note: Clause 'MUST discard': a Prefix-SID kept from an unconfigured EBGP peer goes red at reactor/rfc8669_test.go::TestRFC8669PrefixSIDFromEBGPDiscardedByDefault assert.False(found) after enforceRFC7606, and for repeated copies at rfc8669_multi_test.go::TestRFC8669PrefixSIDEveryOccurrenceDiscardedFromEBGP. Clause 'unless configured': an over-firing strip goes red at TestRFC8669PrefixSIDFromEBGPAcceptedWhenConfigured assert.True(found); IBGP not affected is pinned in TestRFC8669PrefixSIDKeptPathsKeepExactlyOneCopy.

RFC8669-4-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-15 after f49cfab6e7 by an auditor who authored none of 2f0b126768, c9c935547a, f49cfab6e7. RFC 8669 Section 4: "A BGP speaker receiving a BGP Prefix-SID attribute from an External BGP (EBGP) neighbor residing outside the boundaries of the SR domain MUST discard the attribute unless it is configured to accept the attribute from the EBGP neighbor.  A BGP speaker SHOULD log an error for further analysis when discarding an attribute." Producer: validateRFC7606Attrs raises the boundary discard after the walk and records it with AddDiscard even when an earlier discard took result.AttrCode; logRFC7606Discards logs it. Positives: TestRFC8669EBGPBoundaryDiscardLoggedAtDefaultLevel (rfc8669EBGPSession(false), well-formed Label-Index; one ERROR, attr=40, event, peer) and, new, the EBGP boundary case of TestRFC8669PrefixSIDDiscardBesideAnotherLogsBoth (one-octet ATOMIC_AGGREGATE discarded in the walk, so code 6 is result.AttrCode; exactly one attr=40 record citing RFC 8669, whose reason is the boundary description, and one attr=6 record). Negative: TestRFC8669EBGPAcceptedPrefixSIDNoErrorLog (same body on rfc8669EBGPSession(true); ActionNone, no attr=40 ERROR), recorded by the ActionNone-logging mutant of applyRFC7606 instead of a crash; the ignore-accept mutant reddens it on the action assertion first and is evidence of the boundary rule only, not of the log. Independent overlay probes: M1, M7 and M8 redden the EBGP case; M6 (boundary AddDiscard only when it took result.AttrCode, the c9c935547a fix undone) reddens the EBGP case alone, which is exactly the shape this requirement owns; baseline green.

RFC8669-4.1-15.note: Re-judged 2026-10-15 after f49cfab6e7 by an auditor who authored none of 2f0b126768, c9c935547a, f49cfab6e7. RFC 8669 Section 4.1: "In the case of an "invalid" BGP Prefix-SID attribute, a BGP speaker MUST follow the error-handling rules specified in Section 6.  A BGP speaker SHOULD log an error for further analysis." and "A BGP Prefix-SID attribute received without a Label-Index TLV MUST be considered to be "invalid" by the receiving speaker." Producer: validatePrefixSIDForRoutes then validatePrefixSIDValue map PrefixSIDInvalidAttribute to attribute-discard after the walk; logRFC7606Discards logs each discarded code with its own reason. Positives: TestRFC8669InvalidPrefixSIDLoggedAtDefaultLevel (only an Originator SRGB TLV on IPv4 labeled unicast, so the sole fault is the missing Label-Index; one ERROR, attr=40, 'no Label-Index TLV') and, new, TestRFC8669InvalidPrefixSIDDiscardBesideAnotherLogsBoth (the same invalid attribute with a one-octet ATOMIC_AGGREGATE before and after it; one attr=40 record naming the missing Label-Index, one attr=6 record that does not). This closes the earlier finding that no test co-discarded an INVALID Prefix-SID: its record is the M1 mutant of logRFC7606Discards. Negative: TestRFC8669CleanPrefixSIDNoErrorLog (Label-Index present, ActionNone, no attr=40 ERROR), recorded by a mutant that logs attr 40 on the ActionNone return of applyRFC7606, so the negative now discriminates a spurious log rather than reachability. Independent overlay probes: M1, M7 (log only the first entry) and M8 (one rate-limit window shared by all codes) redden both Invalid BesideAnother cases; baseline green. The positive is a genuinely invalid, not malformed, input: the SRGB TLV is well-formed and the asserted reason is the Label-Index one.

RFC8669-6-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-14 (independent reader, after 8c1c4013f2 and 7d37dcd562). RFC 8669 Section 6, malformed or invalid attribute on IPv4/IPv6 labeled unicast: 'it MUST ignore the received BGP Prefix-SID attribute and not advertise it to other BGP peers.' The three RA findings are answered. TLV length constraints: TestRFC8669LabelIndexLengthMalformedOnLabeledUnicast (Label-Index 6 and 8, both families, attribute 40 before and after MP_REACH_NLRI) and TestRFC8669SRGBLengthMalformedOnLabeledUnicast (2, 3, 9) assert attribute-discard of exactly code 40. Minimum attribute length: TestRFC8669EmptyAttributeMalformed asserts attribute-discard of code 40. Positive: TestRFC8669ConformingTLVLengthsAcceptedOnLabeledUnicast asserts no action for Label-Index 7 alone and with SRGB 8 or 14. 'Not advertise': prefixsid-malformed-receive.ci, octet for octet, relays (a) Label-Index 6, (d) no Label-Index (the 'invalid' case, RFC 8669 Section 4.1) and (e1) empty attribute on IPv4 labeled unicast with attribute 40 absent, replaced by an ATTR_TOMBSTONE (type 252) naming code 40. The earlier overrun and trailing-byte units still assert discard. Producer: ClassifyPrefixSID via validatePrefixSIDValue. Rejudged 2026-10-16 (independent reader) after the owner-approved 2026-10-16 change ("5 RFC") to test/plugin/prefixsid-malformed-receive.ci: the only edit is frame (b2), the relayed MP_UNREACH_NLRI for 10.0.2.0/24 RD 65001:1 on IPv4 VPN, whose 3-octet label field now pins 800000 in place of the received 007D01, plus its comment; every other action and expect line is byte-identical. RFC 8277 Section 2.4: "Upon transmission, the Compatibility field SHOULD be set to 0x800000. Upon reception, the value of the Compatibility field MUST be ignored." This row rests on frames (a), (d) and (e1) (IPv4 labeled unicast relayed with attribute 40 replaced by an ATTR_TOMBSTONE naming code 40) and on the message units, none of which changed; (b2) is an IPv4 VPN withdrawal, outside the labeled-unicast scope of this row. RFC 8669 Section 6: "it MUST ignore the received BGP Prefix-SID attribute and not advertise it to other BGP peers." Verdict stands.

RFC8669-6-3.note: Re-judged after 465af38f1d against rfc/full/rfc8669.txt Sections 3, 3.1, 3.2 and 6 and rfc/full/rfc9252.txt Section 7. Positive TestRFC8669DuplicateServiceTLVDiscardedOnReceive drives the real receive entry (enforceRFC7606 to publishBase) on an internal and a route-server-client session and asserts no error, RFC7606ActionNone, exactly one attribute 40 equal to the received TLVs less the repeat in received order, the peer's header width, the received attributes after code 40 octet for octet, and the same TLVs on the forward path; its cases are repeated SRv6 L3 and L2 Service TLVs on labelled unicast, Label-Index twice with an unknown TLV between, an unknown TLV after the repeat, a COMMUNITIES attribute after code 40, an Extended Length header, and L3 Service twice on IPv4 unicast (RFC 9252 Section 7 names no family). Negative TestRFC8669SingleOccurrencePrefixSIDKeptWhole pins the 'only allows for a single occurrence' qualifier and the Section 6 MUST 'unknown TLVs MUST be ignored and propagated unmodified': each type once, an unknown TLV twice, an Originator SRGB TLV twice (Section 3.2 'MUST NOT be changed during the propagation', so keeping both copies is the conforming answer) and a Label-Index TLV twice on IPv4 unicast must publish the received body octet-equal and forward every TLV. test/plugin/prefixsid-duplicate-tlv-relay.ci proves the session-in to session-out path with two byte-identical controls (unknown repeat; Label-Index repeat off labelled unicast) and an L3 Service repeat trimmed with the trailing unknown TLV and COMMUNITIES kept. The judge ran five -overlay mutants on HEAD, none recorded: Label-Index single on every family, stop copying after the first discard, family always read as IPv4 unicast, Extended Length header read as 3 octets, and the attributes after code 40 dropped; each turned a tagged reactor test red. Recorded discrimination records cover all three reactor/.ci tags (producer disabled). Readings, not findings: RFC 8669 sets no explicit occurrence limit for Label-Index; Ze treats it as single on IPv4/IPv6 labelled unicast from 'the label index for a given prefix', and off labelled unicast, where Section 3.1 says it 'MUST be ignored when received for other BGP AFI/SAFI combinations', as unrecognized and propagated unmodified (owner decision 2026-10-03). This is a defensible reading of an RFC that is silent, not RFC text. An UPDATE carrying both RFC 4271 NLRI and an MP_REACH_NLRI is judged by the MP_REACH family (prefixSIDRouteFamily), and no test covers it. The pool pair TestRFC8669DuplicateRecognizedTLVFirstWins / CannotOverrideFirst is one read-side first-wins assertion wearing two hats (the SIDs are swapped), so the polarity pair rests on the reactor and .ci tests, not on these two. A malformed repeat stays treat-as-withdraw first (untagged TestRFC8669DuplicateMalformedServiceTLVStillWithdrawn), which is RFC 9252 Section 7 and outside this row. Re-judged 2026-10-14 (independent reader, after 8c1c4013f2 and 7d37dcd562). Both units' labeled-unicast cases now lead with a Label-Index TLV, because a labeled-unicast Prefix-SID without one is invalid (Section 4.1) and would be discarded before the repeat rule is reached; the assertions are unchanged, so each buffer still isolates this rule. Verdict unchanged.

RFC8669-6-4.note: Re-judged 2026-10-15 after f49cfab6e7 by an auditor who authored none of 2f0b126768, c9c935547a, f49cfab6e7. RFC 8669 Section 6: "This is equivalent to the "Attribute discard" action specified in [RFC7606].  When discarding an attribute, a BGP speaker SHOULD log an error for further analysis." Read as binding the attribute discard of the paragraph it closes (malformed or invalid code 40 on labeled unicast); the RFC 7606 Section 3.g keep-first strip of a repeated code 40 (next paragraph, row 6-2) logs only at Debug and is not judged here. Positives: TestRFC8669PrefixSIDDiscardLoggedAtDefaultLevel (TLV overrun, trailing bytes; exactly one ERROR, attr=40, attr-name, event, description, peer, at slogutil.DefaultLevel) and, new, TestRFC8669PrefixSIDDiscardBesideAnotherLogsBoth (TLV overrun with a one-octet ATOMIC_AGGREGATE before and after code 40, plus the EBGP boundary case; exactly one attr=40 record citing RFC 8669 and one attr=6 record that does not), with TestRFC8669MalformedPrefixSIDDiscardDiagnostic keeping the Debug detail. Negatives: TestRFC8669CleanPrefixSIDNoErrorLog (well-formed Label-Index, ActionNone, no attr=40 ERROR) and TestRFC8669CleanPrefixSIDNoDiscardDiagnostic. The weak finding of 452cfef3db/d16c1740fa is closed: the multi-discard unit is now tagged and fingerprinted, its record is the M1 mutant (logRFC7606Discards logs result.AttrCode/result.Description, the pre-c9c935547a behaviour), and the negative's record is a mutant that logs attr 40 on the ActionNone return of applyRFC7606, not a crash. Independent overlay probes (go test -overlay under ./le job run, tree untouched, baseline green): M1 reddens all three BesideAnother cases and both Invalid BesideAnother cases; M7 (log only the first discard entry) reddens the same five; M6 (EBGP boundary AddDiscard only when it took result.AttrCode) reddens the EBGP case; M8 (one rate-limit window shared by all codes) reddens all five BesideAnother cases. Isolation holds: the ATOMIC_AGGREGATE-before ordering makes code 6 result.AttrCode so a first-only log loses attr=40, and the reason assertions catch a record carrying the other attribute's description. Residual, not a finding: records of one code from one peer are rate-limited to one per second with a suppressed count, which keeps the evidence for analysis.
